numeric.name: driver_age
numeric.description: Age of the primary driver in years; a fundamental risk factor capturing young/inexperienced and elderly driver risk profiles.

numeric.name: vehicle_age
numeric.description: Age of the insured vehicle in years; older vehicles typically have lower values but higher mechanical failure risk and different repair cost profiles.
numeric.data_quality_note: Max of 68 years is plausible for classic/vintage vehicles but worth validating against vehicle_value for consistency.

numeric.name: age_driving_licence
numeric.description: Number of years the driver has held a licence; proxy for driving experience, correlated with but distinct from driver_age.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0 may indicate newly licensed drivers; values should be cross-checked against driver_age for logical consistency (licence age cannot exceed driver_age minus ~16).

numeric.name: vehicle_value
numeric.description: Market or insured value of the vehicle in currency units; key driver of comprehensive/property damage premium and theft exposure.
numeric.data_quality_note: 0.14% nulls require imputation; max of ~374k suggests high-value/exotic vehicles — consider capping or log-transforming to reduce leverage.

numeric.name: power_to_weight_ratio
numeric.description: Engine power relative to vehicle weight; proxy for vehicle performance and associated accident severity/frequency risk.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0 may indicate missing or electric vehicles with no combustion engine — verify these records.

numeric.name: seats
numeric.description: Number of seats in the vehicle; relates to occupant exposure and vehicle category (passenger car vs. minibus).
numeric.data_quality_note: Low cardinality (8 unique values); could be treated as categorical but numeric encoding is appropriate for GBM.

numeric.name: liability_premium
numeric.description: Current booked liability premium component; reflects existing pricing signal and risk segmentation already embedded in the tariff.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0 may indicate policies where liability cover is not applicable (e.g., TP-only variants) — verify against policy_type.

numeric.name: property_damage_premium
numeric.description: Current booked own-damage/property premium component; captures existing pricing for physical damage coverage.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0 expected for policies without own-damage cover; high std relative to mean suggests skewed distribution.

numeric.name: theft_premium
numeric.description: Current booked theft premium component; reflects theft risk pricing already embedded in the tariff.
numeric.data_quality_note: Min of 0 expected for policies without theft cover.

numeric.name: glass_premium
numeric.description: Current booked glass/windscreen premium component; reflects glass breakage risk pricing.

numeric.name: legal_protection_premium
numeric.description: Current booked legal protection premium component; reflects legal expenses cover pricing.

numeric.name: occupants_premium
numeric.description: Current booked occupants/personal accident premium component; reflects cover for vehicle occupants.

numeric.name: fire_premium
numeric.description: Current booked fire premium component; reflects fire damage risk pricing.

categorical.name: policy_type
categorical.description: Type of motor insurance policy (e.g., comprehensive, third-party); directly determines which coverages are included and is a primary risk/premium driver.
categorical.data_quality_note: Ordering is approximate from least to most comprehensive coverage; CC vs COMP_N/COMP_E ordering should be validated against actual coverage definitions.

categorical.name: business_type
categorical.description: Indicates whether the policy is new business (NB) or a renewal/portfolio transfer (P); renewal business typically has lower risk due to selection effects.

categorical.name: payment_frequency
categorical.description: Frequency of premium payment (Annual, Semi-annual, Quarterly); more frequent payment may correlate with financial stress and higher lapse/risk profiles.

categorical.name: bonus_score
categorical.description: Bonus-malus or no-claims discount score (Good, Neutral, Bad); direct indicator of historical claims experience and future risk.
categorical.data_quality_note: Highly imbalanced — 'B' and 'N' categories are small; ensure sufficient credibility for model learning.

categorical.name: fuel_type
categorical.description: Type of fuel used by the vehicle (Diesel, Gasoline); associated with vehicle usage patterns, engine type, and repair cost differences.
categorical.data_quality_note: 0.36% nulls require imputation or a missing indicator; consider whether missing fuel type correlates with electric/hybrid vehicles.

categorical.name: vehicle_brand
categorical.description: Manufacturer/brand of the insured vehicle; captures brand-level differences in repair costs, theft attractiveness, and driver demographics.
categorical.data_quality_note: 68 unique brands with varying exposure volumes; low-frequency brands may need grouping to avoid overfitting.

categorical.name: municipality_type
categorical.description: Classification of the municipality where the vehicle is registered (e.g., Interior, Capital, Island); proxy for traffic density and accident/theft risk.

categorical.name: circulation_area
categorical.description: Urban or rural circulation area of the vehicle; urban areas typically exhibit higher frequency of minor accidents and theft.

exclusion_rationale.policy_status: Active/cancelled status is an outcome of the policy lifecycle rather than a risk predictor; including it would introduce target leakage as cancelled policies may have different premium structures for non-risk reasons.
exclusion_rationale.total_claims: Realised claims count during the exposure period; using it as a feature would constitute target leakage since it is an outcome variable contemporaneous with the premium target.
exclusion_rationale.liability_claims: Realised liability claims count; target leakage — outcome variable that should not be used as a predictor of premium.
exclusion_rationale.liability_property_claims: Realised liability property damage claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.liability_injury_claims: Realised liability bodily injury claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.property_claims: Realised own-damage property claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.theft_claims: Realised theft claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.fire_claims: Realised fire claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.glass_claims: Realised glass claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.legal_protection_claims: Realised legal protection claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.occupants_claims: Realised occupants/personal accident claims count; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.total_incurred: Total incurred claims cost during the exposure period; direct outcome variable — using it would constitute severe target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.liability_incurred: Incurred liability claims cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.liability_property_incurred: Incurred liability property damage cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.liability_injury_incurred: Incurred liability bodily injury cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.property_incurred: Incurred own-damage property cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.theft_incurred: Incurred theft claims cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.fire_incurred: Incurred fire claims cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.glass_incurred: Incurred glass claims cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.legal_protection_incurred: Incurred legal protection claims cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.occupants_incurred: Incurred occupants/personal accident claims cost; target leakage.
exclusion_rationale.liability_exposure: Exposure measure for the liability coverage sub-period; this is an exposure variable analogous to total_exposure and should be used in model offsets if needed, not as a feature, to avoid confounding the exposure structure.

terms.name: driver_age
terms.rationale: Driver age is one of the most fundamental rating factors in motor insurance. Younger drivers (<25) and older drivers (>70) exhibit significantly higher claim frequencies and severities due to inexperience and declining reaction times respectively. A spline or banded transformation is recommended to capture the non-linear U-shaped risk curve.

terms.name: vehicle_age
terms.rationale: Vehicle age affects both claim frequency and severity. Older vehicles tend to have lower market values (reducing property damage severity) but may have higher mechanical failure rates. It also correlates with safety feature availability (ABS, airbags, ADAS). A monotone or banded effect is actuarially expected.

terms.name: age_driving_licence
terms.rationale: Years of driving experience is a strong predictor of claim frequency, particularly for newly licensed drivers. It complements driver_age by capturing experience independently of age (e.g., a 40-year-old who recently obtained a licence). A decreasing risk curve with increasing licence age is expected.

terms.name: vehicle_value
terms.rationale: Vehicle value is a primary driver of claim severity for own-damage, theft, and fire coverages. Higher-value vehicles generate larger repair and replacement costs. A log-linear or banded relationship with total premium is actuarially standard and regulatorily well-accepted.

terms.name: power_to_weight_ratio
terms.rationale: Power-to-weight ratio is a proxy for vehicle performance and driving aggressiveness. Higher ratios are associated with greater speeding risk and accident severity. This is a well-established technical rating factor used across European motor markets.

terms.name: seats
terms.rationale: Number of seats is a proxy for vehicle type (passenger car vs. minivan vs. commercial vehicle) and potential occupant exposure. It influences occupant injury premiums and overall risk profile. Typically enters as a categorical or banded variable.

terms.name: liability_premium
terms.rationale: The liability sub-premium reflects the underwriter's assessment of third-party bodily injury and property risk for this policy. Including it as an offset or predictor captures coverage-specific risk loading and ensures consistency between sub-line pricing and total premium.

terms.name: property_damage_premium
terms.rationale: Property damage sub-premium encodes own-damage risk assessment. It is a key component of total premium and its inclusion ensures the GLM respects the additive structure of coverage-level pricing while allowing for portfolio-level adjustments.

terms.name: theft_premium
terms.rationale: Theft sub-premium captures vehicle theft risk, which varies significantly by vehicle brand, value, municipality type, and circulation area. Including it as a main effect ensures theft risk is properly reflected in total premium.

terms.name: glass_premium
terms.rationale: Glass damage is a high-frequency, low-severity coverage. The glass sub-premium reflects windscreen and glazing risk, which varies by vehicle type and usage. It contributes meaningfully to total premium volume and should be retained as a main effect.

terms.name: legal_protection_premium
terms.rationale: Legal protection coverage premium reflects the risk of legal disputes arising from motor incidents. It varies by policy type and business use. Including it as a main effect maintains consistency with sub-line pricing architecture.

terms.name: occupants_premium
terms.rationale: Occupants coverage premium reflects personal accident risk for vehicle occupants. It is influenced by number of seats, usage type, and business context. A strong main effect is expected and actuarially justified.

terms.name: fire_premium
terms.rationale: Fire coverage premium captures vehicle fire risk, which correlates with vehicle age, fuel type, and vehicle value. It is a standard motor coverage component and its main effect is well-supported actuarially.

terms.name: policy_type
terms.rationale: Policy type (e.g., third-party only, third-party fire and theft, comprehensive) is a fundamental rating dimension that determines which coverages are active. It has a direct structural impact on total premium and is universally used in motor pricing.

terms.name: business_type
terms.rationale: Business type distinguishes personal from commercial use, fleet from individual policies, etc. Commercial and fleet use typically exhibit different risk profiles (higher mileage, different driver pools). This is a standard and regulatorily accepted rating factor.

terms.name: payment_frequency
terms.rationale: Payment frequency (annual, semi-annual, monthly) is associated with policyholder financial behaviour and retention risk. Monthly payers tend to exhibit higher lapse rates and sometimes different risk profiles. It also captures instalment loading in premium. Actuarially justified as a main effect.

terms.name: bonus_score
terms.rationale: Bonus-malus score (or no-claims discount level) is one of the most predictive variables in motor insurance, directly reflecting individual claims history. It is universally used across European markets and is strongly actuarially and regulatorily justified.

terms.name: fuel_type
terms.rationale: Fuel type (petrol, diesel, electric, hybrid, LPG) affects fire risk, repair costs, and vehicle performance characteristics. Electric vehicles in particular have different repair cost profiles. A categorical main effect is actuarially justified.

terms.name: vehicle_brand
terms.rationale: Vehicle brand is a proxy for repair cost, parts availability, theft attractiveness, and safety ratings. It is a standard motor rating factor. Should be encoded as grouped categories (e.g., premium, standard, budget) or with credibility smoothing to avoid overfitting sparse brands.

terms.name: municipality_type
terms.rationale: Municipality type (urban, suburban, rural) captures geographic risk variation in accident frequency, theft rates, and traffic density. It is a well-established territorial rating factor and is regulatorily accepted as a proxy for geographic risk without using individual postcodes.

terms.name: circulation_area
terms.rationale: Circulation area captures the broader geographic zone of vehicle operation, complementing municipality type with regional risk differences (e.g., weather, road infrastructure, regional claim cost levels). Standard territorial rating factor in motor pricing.

terms.name: payment_frequency:bonus_score
terms.rationale: The strongest interaction in the GBM. Actuarially plausible: policyholders with poor bonus scores (high risk) who pay monthly may represent a distinct adverse selection segment — higher-risk individuals who cannot afford annual payment. The interaction captures differential premium loading by payment behaviour conditional on risk history.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.41 is high and warrants inclusion. The interaction is commercially meaningful: monthly payers with low bonus scores may be systematically underpriced if only main effects are used. Recommend validating with lift charts segmented by payment_frequency x bonus_score band before finalising relativities.

terms.name: occupants_premium:business_type
terms.rationale: Occupants coverage risk varies substantially by business type: commercial vehicles carry more passengers more frequently, and employer liability considerations differ from personal use. The interaction between occupants sub-premium and business type is actuarially well-motivated and reflects genuine structural differences in exposure.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.34 is strong. This interaction is defensible: the occupants premium loading should differ between personal and commercial/fleet policies. Ensure the interaction is parameterised consistently with the occupants coverage underwriting rules.

terms.name: property_damage_premium:liability_premium
terms.rationale: Property damage and liability sub-premiums are both driven by at-fault accident risk. Their interaction captures the joint effect of policies where both coverages are active and correlated — e.g., comprehensive policies where a single at-fault accident triggers both liability and own-damage claims. Actuarially justified as a bundling effect.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.30 is material. The interaction reflects the correlation between third-party and own-damage risk for the same driver. However, care is needed to avoid double-counting with policy_type main effect. Recommend checking VIF and partial dependence plots.

terms.name: vehicle_value:bonus_score
terms.rationale: High-value vehicles driven by high-risk drivers (low bonus score) represent a compounded risk: both higher severity and higher frequency. The interaction captures the non-additive effect where a poor claims history on an expensive vehicle warrants a super-additive premium loading beyond the sum of individual effects.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.29 is material and the interaction is actuarially intuitive. Regulatorily defensible as it reflects genuine risk compounding. Recommend banding vehicle_value into quantile groups for the interaction term to improve stability.

terms.name: fire_premium:bonus_score
terms.rationale: Fire risk and claims history interact: policyholders with poor bonus scores may also exhibit riskier vehicle storage and usage behaviours that elevate fire risk. The interaction captures this behavioural correlation between general risk propensity (bonus score) and fire-specific risk.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.28 is notable. The actuarial rationale is plausible but somewhat indirect — bonus score primarily reflects accident history, not fire behaviour. Recommend including but monitoring for overfitting. Consider whether the signal persists after controlling for vehicle_age and fuel_type.

terms.name: bonus_score:vehicle_age
terms.rationale: Older vehicles combined with poor bonus scores may indicate a segment of high-risk drivers operating older, potentially less safe vehicles — a compounded risk profile. Conversely, good bonus score drivers with older vehicles may represent low-risk, low-mileage usage. The interaction captures this segmentation.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.27 is material. Actuarially justified: the combination of vehicle age and claims history provides meaningful risk segmentation. Recommend validating that the interaction is not confounded with vehicle_value (older vehicles tend to be lower value).

terms.name: legal_protection_premium:business_type
terms.rationale: Legal protection risk differs fundamentally between personal and commercial/fleet policies. Commercial policyholders face employer liability, contractual disputes, and regulatory proceedings that personal policyholders do not. The interaction between legal protection sub-premium and business type is structurally justified.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.27 is strong and the interaction is actuarially and regulatorily defensible. Ensure the interaction relativities are consistent with the legal protection product terms for commercial vs. personal policies.

terms.name: vehicle_age:driver_age
terms.rationale: Young drivers in older vehicles represent a well-documented high-risk segment: older vehicles lack modern safety features (ABS, ESC, airbags) and young drivers have higher accident frequency. This interaction is actuarially classic and regulatorily well-accepted across European motor markets.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.13 is moderate but the actuarial rationale is very strong and well-documented in motor insurance literature. This interaction should be retained on actuarial grounds even if the H-statistic alone would not prioritise it highly. Recommend banding both variables for the interaction term.

terms.name: policy_type:payment_frequency
terms.rationale: The relationship between payment frequency and premium loading may differ by policy type. Comprehensive policyholders paying monthly may represent a different risk and retention profile than third-party-only monthly payers. The interaction captures differential instalment behaviour by coverage level.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.13 is moderate. The interaction is commercially plausible. Recommend validating with observed loss ratios segmented by policy_type x payment_frequency before including in production model.

terms.name: payment_frequency:driver_age
terms.rationale: Young drivers who pay monthly may represent an adverse selection segment: financially constrained high-risk drivers. Older drivers paying monthly may reflect different behaviour (e.g., pensioners on fixed income). The interaction captures age-conditional payment behaviour effects on risk.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.12 is moderate. The actuarial rationale is plausible but the interaction may partially overlap with payment_frequency:bonus_score. Recommend checking for collinearity between these two interactions before including both.

terms.name: driver_age:glass_premium
terms.rationale: Glass claim frequency varies by driver age: younger drivers may be more likely to drive in conditions leading to stone chip damage, while older drivers may be more cautious. The interaction between driver age and glass sub-premium captures age-conditional glass risk loading.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.12 is moderate. The actuarial rationale is plausible but glass claims are high-frequency low-severity and may introduce noise. Recommend validating with observed glass claim rates by driver age band before including.

terms.name: theft_premium:payment_frequency
terms.rationale: Theft risk and payment frequency may interact through geographic and socioeconomic factors: monthly payers in high-theft areas may represent a correlated risk segment. The interaction captures this conditional effect.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.12 is moderate. The actuarial rationale is indirect — payment frequency is not a direct driver of theft risk. This interaction may be partially spurious or driven by confounding with municipality_type. Recommend including only if it survives a partial dependence validation and does not conflict with regulatory guidance on socioeconomic proxies.

terms.name: bonus_score:driver_age
terms.rationale: Young drivers with poor bonus scores represent the highest-risk motor segment. However, young drivers have limited bonus history, so the interaction also captures the credibility of the bonus score signal by age. Actuarially well-motivated and commonly used in European bonus-malus systems.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.11 is moderate but the actuarial rationale is strong. This interaction is standard in markets with bonus-malus systems. Recommend including with appropriate banding of driver_age.

terms.name: property_damage_premium:policy_type
terms.rationale: Property damage coverage is only fully active under comprehensive and TPFT policies. The interaction between property damage sub-premium and policy type captures the structural difference in how property damage risk is priced across coverage tiers.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.11 is moderate. This interaction has a clear structural justification: property damage premiums should be interpreted differently depending on whether the policy includes own-damage coverage. Recommend including as it improves model consistency with product structure.

terms.name: vehicle_value:policy_type
terms.rationale: Vehicle value has different implications depending on policy type: for comprehensive policies it drives own-damage severity directly, while for third-party-only policies its effect is more indirect. The interaction captures this structural difference in how vehicle value translates to premium by coverage tier.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.105 is at the threshold. The actuarial rationale is sound and the interaction is regulatorily defensible. Recommend including.

terms.name: liability_premium:policy_type
terms.rationale: Liability coverage is mandatory across all policy types but its loading differs by coverage tier. The interaction between liability sub-premium and policy type captures differential liability risk pricing by product structure.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.102 is at the threshold. The interaction is structurally justified by product design. Recommend including but monitoring for collinearity with property_damage_premium:policy_type.

terms.name: payment_frequency:business_type
terms.rationale: Commercial policyholders paying monthly may represent different cash flow management practices compared to personal policyholders. The interaction captures differential payment behaviour effects on risk by business type.
terms.actuary_note: H-statistic of 0.101 is at the threshold. The actuarial rationale is plausible but indirect. This interaction may overlap with occupants_premium:business_type. Recommend including provisionally and reviewing in model validation.
